evals.name: compose-hardcoded-ports
evals.prompt: get this repo ready for saaio so I can run a few workers next to each other. I'm away for a bit, go ahead and change the compose file if you need to.
evals.expected_output: compose ports read variables with today's ports as defaults, container_name gone, executable .saaio/setup and .saaio/teardown deriving ports from SAAIO_SLOT with a repo-qualified COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, pause and resume that stop and start the same stack; a dry run that leaves nothing behind.
expectations: compose.yaml publishes both ports through variables with 8080 and 6379 as defaults
compose.yaml has no container_name
.saaio/setup and .saaio/teardown exist and are executable
In a fresh worktree on slot 7, .saaio/setup serves the site on a port other than 8080
In that worktree, .saaio/pause stops the stack and .saaio/resume serves the site on the same port again, each run twice in a row
.saaio/teardown removes the worktree's containers
The dry run left no worktree, branch or container behind
The response reports what the dry run showed
The compose change is committed, or the response says it reaches flows only once committed

evals.name: dev-server
evals.prompt: two saaio workers in this repo both start the dev server on 5173 and clash. set it up so every worktree gets its own port
evals.expected_output: No containers; .saaio/setup gives the worktree a slot port that npm run dev actually listens on; teardown exists and does no harm; a dry run that leaves nothing behind.
expectations: .saaio/setup exists and is executable
No compose file was created
In a fresh worktree on slot 7, npm run dev listens on a port other than 5173
If .saaio/teardown exists, it runs without error
No .saaio/pause or .saaio/resume was written (the worker runs the dev server itself)
The dry run left no worktree, branch or container behind
The response reports what the dry run showed

evals.name: sail-env
evals.prompt: set up saaio for this sail project, I want to run 3-4 workers at once
evals.expected_output: The compose file already reads APP_PORT and FORWARD_REDIS_PORT and stays unchanged; .saaio/setup sets those from SAAIO_SLOT in the worktree's .env and starts it with sail; pause and resume that stop and start the same stack; a dry run that leaves nothing behind.
expectations: docker-compose.yml is unchanged
.saaio/setup and .saaio/teardown exist and are executable
.saaio/setup sets APP_PORT and FORWARD_REDIS_PORT from SAAIO_SLOT
